transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-12
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Jordan (Lyra Head of ML), Priya (Lyra Platform), Owen (Lyra CISO), Tara (Lyra Product)

[00:00:05] Samira: alright thanks everyone for joining, um we'll run through the update, get alignment on SLAs and next steps. quick check — everyone can hear okay?
[00:00:14] Jordan: yep good here
[00:00:17] Owen: good
[00:00:20] Samira: awesome. Maya and Diego from our side — we'll kick with a short recap then dive into the SLA draft. Diego you want to start with the operational notes?
[00:00:30] Diego: yeah, sure. so uh high level — Lyra's production traffic profile we saw from Priya last week is very spiky, two peak windows and lots of mid-sized sessions. average seq length is around 420 tokens but the chat sessions have long tails. that makes batching plus KV-cache behavior important, and also why you saw some elevated p90s in the last report.
[00:01:05] Priya: yeah those tails are mostly from multi-turn customer support sessions, and some generative summaries that hit longer contexts. we profiled a day — can send the trace file after.
[00:01:15] Diego: please, that helps. on the infra choices — given the spikiness our recommendation remains hybrid: dedicated pools for your high-throughput chat routes to hit stable latency and predictable cost, plus hosted routes for experimental models and burst. dedicated lets you pin model variants and preserve KV in memory which reduces token cost for multi-turn.
[00:01:42] Jordan: curious — what are we trading off in cost if we move more into dedicated? at what utilization does dedicated start to pay off?
[00:01:51] Diego: good question. rough rule of thumb — if sustained utilization for a route exceeds ~40-50% of a reserved GPU pool, dedicated becomes more cost-effective. but the exact breakpoint depends on batch sizes, model choice, and quantization profile. we can run a tailored calc with your traces.
[00:02:12] Samira: i'll put that in the action items — diego will run a dedicated vs hosted throughput benchmark using your traces.
[00:02:18] Tara: we also need to confirm latency SLOs — our product team wants p99 under 220ms for the core chat experience. is that realistic?
[00:02:26] Diego: p99 220ms is tight depending on model, sequence length, and whether you need streaming. with a compiled LLM variant, optimized kernels, and reserved capacity we can often meet sub-200ms for 1k token requests on modern GPUs. however, with your long-tail sessions (4-5k tokens) p99 will be higher due to generation time. caching reduces tail but not for brand new contexts.
[00:02:54] Owen: from security perspective we also need deterministic availability — we don't want frequent fallbacks to lower-fidelity models without audit trails.
[00:03:03] Maya: that's a good callout. our rollouts support automatic fallback with traceability — every fallback event is logged and tied to the request id. we can surface those in the console and stream audit logs to your SIEM.
[00:03:18] Owen: great, can you confirm log format and retention? we need logs to be available for 1 year for audit.
[00:03:25] Maya: yes. we have configurable retention; for Private deployments we can match your retention and make logs available via S3 or your SIEM endpoint. for Hosted we have tiered retention options and can ship to your archive. i'll include this in the SLA writeup.
[00:03:39] Owen: also KMS — keys must remain under our control, and HSM backed where possible. any constraints?
[00:03:46] Samira: for Private deployments you can bring-your-own keys (BYOK) and integrate with HSM/KMS; for Dedicated we offer customer KMS integration with envelope encryption to satisfy that. for Hosted we can integrate with customer-managed keys as well, but there are some network placement constraints depending on region.
[00:04:05] Priya: does the BYOK path require us to be on Private or can Dedicated also work?
[00:04:10] Samira: Dedicated can be configured to use your KMS in most cases, yes. Private is used when you also need VPC isolation or air-gapped options.
[00:04:18] Jordan: earlier you mentioned quantization. are there quality regressions we should expect if we push to more aggressive quant?
[00:04:25] Diego: short answer: depends. 4-bit post-training quant can materially reduce memory and increase throughput, but for some tasks with subtle token probabilities we do see small quality deltas. our Optimize toolkit will run evals against your prompt set and surface expected deltas. it's usually a win for throughput-heavy routes.
[00:04:44] Jordan: okay so we want Diego to run quality regressions with our eval prompts in addition to latency.
[00:04:48] Diego: yep we'll do both.
[00:04:50] [00:04:57] Tara: can we talk about SLA terms — penalties, uptime? what are you proposing?
[00:05:02] Samira: the draft i sent earlier proposed 99.9% uptime for dedicated pools with credits for breaches and a service credit schedule. for Hosted we had 99.5% as the baseline. we're open to negotiation — curious what Lyra needs for contractual remedies.
[00:05:18] Owen: from security and third-party risk, we need 99.95% for core payments-related flows. that's non-negotiable.
[00:05:26] Samira: understood. we can separate critical routes into a stricter SLA — designate them to dedicated pools with higher commit and different pricing.
[00:05:35] Jordan: what's the lead time for spinning up dedicated pools? we may need to scale before summer.
[00:05:40] Diego: typical provisioning is 48–72 hours for capacity changes on Dedicated, but initial reserved capacity setup with networking can take a couple weeks if we need cross-account VPC peering or vault integrations.
[00:05:53] Priya: the VPC peering bit — we have tight networking controls; we'll need a diagram and network specs.
[00:05:58] Maya: we'll send a detailed network checklist. also, for Private deployments we can ship a deployment manifest that meets on-prem specs.
[00:06:07] Owen: does Redwood support SAML SSO and SCIM for enterprise provisioning?
[00:06:11] Samira: yes SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported, plus RBAC at the token level. we'll include configuration steps in the onboarding docs.
[00:06:20] Tara: pricing — if we move more into Dedicated to hit stricter SLAs, what's the likely cost delta?
[00:06:27] Samira: cost is a function of reserved commit size and utilization. we can present two options: a heavier commit with lower per-token effective cost for core routes, or a lighter commit plus burst credits. i'll model both once Diego has benchmark results.
[00:06:41] Jordan: timeline: we want to be production-ready for payments-related flows by mid-June. is that feasible?
[00:06:48] Diego: feasible if we start provisioning this month — need traces, security checklist, and SLA agreement. provisioning and integration + compliance review — tight but doable.
[00:06:58] [00:07:05] Owen: on the compliance review, we need SOC 2 Type II and ISO statements, and a security questionnaire filled. also, do you support network isolation for keys so that root keys never leave our vault?
[00:07:16] Maya: we can provide SOC2 reports and ISO attestation, and we have a standard security pack. regarding keys — BYOK with HSM ensures root keys remain in your vault; envelope encryption keeps the working keys ephemeral in the runtime. we'll document end-to-end.
[00:07:33] Priya: one more technical — what's the expected cold-start latency when a KV cache is cold and model warm-up occurs? sometimes we saw 400-500ms spikes last month.
[00:07:42] Diego: warm-up depends on model size and whether the sequence includes long context window. we mitigate via pre-warming strategies and continuous batching; cold-start spikes are expected but we can reduce their frequency with warm pools and smarter routing.
[00:07:58] Jordan: can Redwood emit traces to our observability stack for per-request token and latency breakdown?
[00:08:04] Maya: yes, we can stream traces and token-level cost breakdowns to your observability endpoint or S3. we'll add the exact schema to the docs.
[00:08:12] Samira: ok quick recap — action items: Diego run benchmarks + quality regressions; Samira send SLA redline with two pricing models; Priya share traces; Owen share compliance items. Maya schedule security deep-dive. anything else?
[00:08:28] Tara: can you include an example of fallback behavior in the SLA — we need explicit approvals for any silent model downgrades.
[00:08:35] Samira: yes we'll add a clause for explicit approvals and for mandatory audit logging on fallback.
[00:08:41] [00:20:00] [note: mid-meeting there was a brief screen share walking through the SLA draft and the console — transcript auto-missed some lines]
[00:20:12] Diego: i posted the benchmark plan in the chat — two runs: 1) 24-hour synthetic trace with your seq distribution; 2) focused p99 stress with long tails. we'll run on both hosted and dedicated variants and test aggressive quant profiles.
[00:20:30] Jordan: perfect. will Diego need creds to run against a dev copy of our dataset?
[00:20:34] Priya: yes we can spin up a sanitized trace endpoint, i'll send details.
[00:20:38] Diego: thanks.
[00:20:41] [00:35:10] Owen: one question on incident response — what is your escalations matrix? we need a 24/7 SLA for payments incidents and a named on-call at Redwood.
[00:35:18] Maya: we have an enterprise on-call with 15-minute response for Sev 1 and a named escalation contact for customers on an enterprise plan; we'll include names in the contract.
[00:35:27] Owen: and post-incident telemetry — is there automated root-cause histograms exported?
[00:35:31] Diego: yes we can export traces and token-level histograms, and attach the serving telemetry to a postmortem bundle.
[00:35:38] [00:42:50] Jordan: ok i'm a little worried about model regressions when we quantize — can we gate quantization changes behind canary rollouts and prompt-set evals?
[00:42:58] Diego: absolutely. our rollout system supports canaries and A/B which are tied to prompt-based regressions; if you see measurable delta above your threshold we auto-roll back.
[00:43:07] Tara: can that threshold be contractually defined? we want to say max 1% drop in key metric accuracy.
[00:43:13] Samira: we can include an SLO-style quality guardrail, measured against the evaluation set you provide.
[00:43:19] [00:50:02] Samira: any blockers to signing the SLA by end of next week?
[00:50:07] Owen: need to confirm KMS/HSM constraints and the SOC2 evidence first — that's our gating item.
[00:50:13] Jordan: we also want the benchmark results before committing to the larger reserved pool.
[00:50:17] Samira: fair. we'll prioritize Diego's runs and get the SLA redline out.
[00:50:22] Priya: i'll share the traces today and open a ticket for network specs.
[00:50:26] Maya: i'll set up the security deep-dive and send calendar invites.
[00:50:30] [00:56:45] Samira: thanks everyone, i'll summarize in email and share the redline. recap of next steps in chat — Diego, Maya, Samira, Priya, Owen. meeting adjourned.
[00:56:55] Jordan: thanks all
[00:56:57] Owen: thanks

Meeting end.

Notes about transcription: occasional missed words during screenshare and some proper nouns (Lyra internal route names) were auto-transcribed incorrectly. We preserved speaker intent.
